    Multilevel and phylogenetic meta-analysis

    Source: R/meta-regression.R
    meta_multilevel.Rd

    meta_multilevel() fits a three-level meta-analytic model for effect sizes nested in clusters (for example several outcomes per study, or several studies per research group). The marginal variance of the effect sizes is $$V = \mathrm{diag}(v_i) + \sigma^2_{(3)} Z R Z^\top + \sigma^2_{(2)} I,$$ where \(Z\) maps effect sizes to clusters and \(R\) is the identity, or a phylogenetic (or any other known) correlation matrix supplied with cor_matrix. The variance components are estimated by restricted or full maximum likelihood using bounded quasi-Newton optimisation, and the fixed effects by generalised least squares.

    Usage

    meta_multilevel(
  .data,
  cluster,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  within = NULL,
  mods = NULL,
  method = "REML",
  test = "z",
  level = 0.95,
  study = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A <meta_es> from meta_effect_size() or any data frame with effect sizes and sampling variances.

    cluster

    <data-masking> The upper level grouping (level 3), such as study, district or species.

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    within

    <data-masking> Optional identifier of the level 2 units nested in cluster. Defaults to one unit per row (per effect size).

    mods

    An optional one-sided formula of moderators. Defaults to an intercept only model.

    method

    "REML" or "ML".

    test

    "z" or "t" (t tests with \(k - p\) degrees of freedom).

    level

    Confidence level for intervals.

    study

    <data-masking> Optional study labels. Taken from the <meta_es> when available.

    cor_matrix

    An optional correlation matrix among clusters, with row and column names matching the values of cluster. Supply a phylogenetic correlation matrix (for example from ape::vcv(tree, corr = TRUE)) for a phylogenetic meta-analysis.

    Value

    A <meta_fit> with one row per coefficient. The variance components are returned by glance().

    Details

    The \(I^2\) statistics follow Nakagawa and Santos (2012): the share of the total variance due to each random effect, using the typical sampling variance of Higgins and Thompson (2002).

    References

    Konstantopoulos, S. (2011). Fixed effects and variance components estimation in three-level meta-analysis. Research Synthesis Methods, 2(1), 61-76. doi:10.1002/jrsm.35

    Nakagawa, S. and Santos, E. S. A. (2012). Methodological issues and advances in biological meta-analysis. Evolutionary Ecology, 26(5), 1253-1274. doi:10.1007/s10682-012-9555-5

    Hadfield, J. D. and Nakagawa, S. (2010). General quantitative genetic methods for comparative biology: phylogenies, taxonomies and multi-trait models for continuous and categorical characters. Journal of Evolutionary Biology, 23(3), 494-508. doi:10.1111/j.1420-9101.2009.01915.x

    Examples

    fit <- meta_multilevel(school_calendar, yi = yi, vi = vi,
  cluster = district, within = school)
fit
#> # Multilevel meta-analysis <meta_fit>
#> # Model: REML with 2 random effect levels
#> # Measure: generic effect size; k = 56
#> # sigma^2 (district) = 0.0651
#> # sigma^2 (school) = 0.0327
#> # Q(55) = 578.86, p < 0.0001
#> # 95% prediction interval: [-0.4502, 0.8197]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   term    estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 overall    0.185    0.0846      2.18  0.0289   0.0190     0.350
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 25
#>   model_type  nobs method test   tau2 tau2.low tau2.high   tau    I2    H2    R2
#>   <chr>      <int> <chr>  <chr> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 multilevel    56 REML   z        NA       NA        NA    NA  95.2    NA    NA
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: QE <dbl>, df.residual <int>, p.QE <dbl>, QM <dbl>,
#> #   p.QM <dbl>, pred.low <dbl>, pred.high <dbl>, logLik <dbl>, AIC <dbl>,
#> #   BIC <dbl>, sigma2_district <dbl>, I2_district <dbl>, sigma2_school <dbl>,
#> #   I2_school <dbl>
